items.label: f03-rls-layers
items.front: Name Morphic's layered access checks from request to row.
items.back: proxy.ts refreshes the Supabase session; getCurrentUserId resolves the user (or the anonymous id when auth is disabled locally); actions check ownership; withRLS sets app.current_user_id for the transaction so Postgres policies (users_manage_own_chats, public_chats_readable) filter rows.

items.label: f02-persist-order
items.front: In what order does persistStreamResults do its work?
items.back: Await the title promise; await the pending initial chat save (with a createChatWithFirstMessage fallback that tolerates duplicate keys); upsert the assistant message, retrying once through retryDatabaseOperation; then update the title if it is not the default. Errors are logged, not thrown.

items.label: f01-search-page-flow
items.back: SearchPage awaits params, gets the user id, calls loadChat (unstable_cache around loadChatWithMessages under withOptionalRLS), calls notFound() on null, then renders Chat with savedMessages, isGuest and model selector data. Private chats come back null for anyone but their owner.

items.prompt: Tracing is disabled (isTracingEnabled() is false). A valid feedback request arrives with a messageId. What happens to that message's feedback in the database?

choices.text: The score is queued in memory until tracing is turned back on
Nothing is written, and the route answers 200 tracking not enabled
The route answers 503, because tracing is a hard requirement
The score is written to the message, and the Langfuse call is skipped

choices: The score is queued in memory until tracing is turned back on
Nothing is written, and the route answers 200 tracking not enabled
The route answers 503, because tracing is a hard requirement
The score is written to the message, and the Langfuse call is skipped

items.explanation: The tracing check returns 200 "Feedback tracking is not enabled" before both the Langfuse score and updateMessageFeedback, so with tracing off the message metadata is never updated even though a messageId was sent.

items.prompt: How does lib/actions/chat.ts cache the result of loadChat(chatId, requestingUserId)?

choices.text: React cache() for one request, then a fresh database read every time
A module-level Map keyed by chat id that is kept until server restart
unstable_cache keyed by chat id and user, tagged, revalidated after 60 s
No caching: every call opens a new RLS transaction against Postgres

choices: React cache() for one request, then a fresh database read every time
A module-level Map keyed by chat id that is kept until server restart
unstable_cache keyed by chat id and user, tagged, revalidated after 60 s
No caching: every call opens a new RLS transaction against Postgres

items.explanation: getCachedChatWithMessages wraps the DB call in unstable_cache with the key [chat-with-messages, chatId, requestingUserId or anonymous], tags chat-<id> and chat, and revalidate: 60. Mutating actions call revalidateTag to drop it early.

items.prompt: The user stops an authenticated answer mid-stream, so onFinish runs with isAborted true. What happens to the partial assistant message?

choices.text: It is saved, with an aborted flag set on the message row
It is saved as is, with only the text that was streamed so far
It is queued to be saved on the next request
It is not persisted, as onFinish returns before saving

choices: It is saved, with an aborted flag set on the message row
It is saved as is, with only the text that was streamed so far
It is queued to be saved on the next request
It is not persisted, as onFinish returns before saving

items.explanation: onFinish starts with if (isAborted || !responseMessage) return, so persistStreamResults never runs for an aborted stream. The finally block still flushes Langfuse.

items.prompt: In persistStreamResults the initial chat save failed, and the fallback create then fails with a connection error (not a duplicate key). What happens to the assistant response?

choices.text: It is saved anyway, through the retryDatabaseOperation helper
It is rethrown, so the user sees a 500 error in the chat
It is saved to a separate guest table for a later merge
It is dropped; the function logs the error and returns

choices: It is saved anyway, through the retryDatabaseOperation helper
It is rethrown, so the user sees a 500 error in the chat
It is saved to a separate guest table for a later merge
It is dropped; the function logs the error and returns

items.explanation: For a non-duplicate fallback error the code logs "Fallback chat creation failed" and returns, so the upsert and its retry never run. The answer was already streamed to the user, but nothing is stored; the guide flags this swallow-and-log style as a data-loss risk.

items.prompt: After a successful upload, which value does useFileDropzone store as the attachment's name?

choices.text: undefined, as it reads uploaded.name but the route sends filename
The sanitized lowercase name that the route returns as name
The R2 object key, which the route returns as uploaded.name
The original file name, read from the uploaded.filename response field

choices: undefined, as it reads uploaded.name but the route sends filename
The sanitized lowercase name that the route returns as name
The R2 object key, which the route returns as uploaded.name
The original file name, read from the uploaded.filename response field

items.explanation: The hook copies uploaded.url, uploaded.name and uploaded.key, but uploadFileToR2 returns filename, url, mediaType and type. name and key are therefore undefined; this is the response-shape mismatch the mission asks you to find.

items.prompt: A deployment sets ENABLE_AUTH=false and MORPHIC_CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT=true. What does getCurrentUserId do?

choices.text: It throws: ENABLE_AUTH=false is not allowed in cloud
It returns anonymous-user, with a console warning
It ignores ENABLE_AUTH and asks Supabase for the user
It returns undefined; every request is then a guest

choices: It throws: ENABLE_AUTH=false is not allowed in cloud
It returns anonymous-user, with a console warning
It ignores ENABLE_AUTH and asks Supabase for the user
It returns undefined; every request is then a guest

items.explanation: The ENABLE_AUTH === "false" branch first checks the cloud flag and throws an Error with that message. Only on a non-cloud deployment does it warn and return ANONYMOUS_USER_ID or anonymous-user.

items.prompt: A personal Docker deployment sets ENABLE_AUTH=false and does not set ANONYMOUS_USER_ID. Two people use it from two browsers. Which user id do their requests get?

choices.text: Each gets a random id that is stored in its own browser cookie
Both get the same id, the literal anonymous-user
Each gets its own Supabase anonymous session
Both get undefined and are treated as guests

choices: Each gets a random id that is stored in its own browser cookie
Both get the same id, the literal anonymous-user
Each gets its own Supabase anonymous session
Both get undefined and are treated as guests

items.explanation: getCurrentUserId returns process.env.ANONYMOUS_USER_ID || "anonymous-user" in this mode, and the warning says all users share the same user ID. That is why the mode is for personal use only.

items.prompt: A signed-out visitor opens /search/abc, where chat abc exists and has visibility private. What does SearchPage do?

choices.text: It renders the chat read-only with the saved messages
It calls notFound(), so the visitor gets the 404 page
It renders an empty Chat with no saved messages at all
It redirects the visitor to /auth/login; they sign in first

choices: It renders the chat read-only with the saved messages
It calls notFound(), so the visitor gets the 404 page
It renders an empty Chat with no saved messages at all
It redirects the visitor to /auth/login; they sign in first

items.explanation: loadChatWithMessages returns null for a private chat when there is no userId, so SearchPage hits if (!chat) notFound() before its private-chat redirect. The redirect to /auth/login is unreachable for this case; the senior guide lists it as a bug-injection symptom, and the code is keyed here.

items.prompt: POST /api/feedback receives { traceId: "t1", score: 0 }. What does the route answer?

choices.text: 400 score must be 1 (good) or -1 (bad)
400 traceId is required
200 Feedback recorded successfully
422 with a Zod issue list for the score field

choices: 400 score must be 1 (good) or -1 (bad)
400 traceId is required
200 Feedback recorded successfully
422 with a Zod issue list for the score field

items.explanation: traceId is present, so the first check passes; score 0 is neither 1 nor -1, so the second check returns 400. The route validates by hand and never uses Zod, so 422 is not possible here.

items.prompt: In persistStreamResults the initial chat save failed, and the fallback createChatWithFirstMessage then throws a duplicate key error. What happens next?

choices.text: It deletes the chat and creates it again from scratch
It returns without saving the assistant response
It rethrows the error and the stream ends in failure
It treats the chat as existing and saves the response

choices: It deletes the chat and creates it again from scratch
It returns without saving the assistant response
It rethrows the error and the stream ends in failure
It treats the chat as existing and saves the response

items.explanation: A fallback error whose message includes duplicate key or unique constraint is logged as "Chat already exists" and the function continues to upsertMessage. Any other fallback error returns early without saving.

items.prompt: A user already has 2 files attached (maxFiles is 3) and drops 2 more allowed PDFs onto the chat. What does handleDrop do?

choices.text: It uploads the first PDF and silently drops the other
It uploads both and then trims the list to three files
It replaces the two older attachments with the new pair
It shows a maximum-files toast and uploads neither file

choices: It uploads the first PDF and silently drops the other
It uploads both and then trims the list to three files
It replaces the two older attachments with the new pair
It shows a maximum-files toast and uploads neither file

items.explanation: total = uploadedFiles.length + allowed.length is 4, which is greater than maxFiles, so the hook shows "You can upload a maximum of 3 files." and returns before building initialFiles. The later slice(0, maxFiles) only runs when the total fits.

items.prompt: withRLS runs SELECT set_config('app.current_user_id', userId, true) inside db.transaction. What does the final true argument mean?

choices.text: The setting is stored for the whole DB session
The setting lasts only until the transaction ends
The policy is created if it does not exist yet
The user id is checked against the users table

choices: The setting is stored for the whole DB session
The setting lasts only until the transaction ends
The policy is created if it does not exist yet
The user id is checked against the users table

items.explanation: In PostgreSQL, set_config(name, value, is_local) with is_local true behaves like SET LOCAL: the value disappears at the end of the current transaction, so a pooled connection cannot leak one user's id into the next request. The comment in with-rls.ts says the same.

items.prompt: For a new chat, generateChatTitle throws. What title does the chat end up with after persistStreamResults runs?

choices.text: The first 50 characters of the user message text, as typed
The default Untitled title, since the update is skipped
An empty string, as the title column allows it
No title at all; the chat row is rolled back

choices: The first 50 characters of the user message text, as typed
The default Untitled title, since the update is skipped
An empty string, as the title column allows it
No title at all; the chat row is rolled back

items.explanation: The title promise catches the error and resolves to DEFAULT_CHAT_TITLE (Untitled). persistStreamResults only calls updateChatTitle when the title differs from the default, so the chat keeps the title it was created with.
